chunks: I was told by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilawayh, from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Tha'laba ibn Maimun, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said:

Indeed, a man will go out of his home for a need, and he will return whilst not having remembered Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and his journal will be filled with good deeds. He said: So I said: And how is that, may I be sacrificed for you? He said: He will pass by people and they will remember us, the Household, and say: Stop, for indeed, he loves them. Then the Angel will say to his companion: Write the gift of the Family of Muhammad for such-a-person today.

key_terms.هِبَةُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The gift of the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: How can a person earn good deeds without explicitly remembering God?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the profound Shia concept of *hubb al-Ahl al-Bayt* (love for the Prophet's family) as an independent act of worship that carries significant spiritual weight, even when accompanied by other mundane activities. This narration underscores the theological principle that love for the Ahl al-Bayt is intrinsically linked to love for Allah, allowing angels to record such interactions as divine gifts (*hibat*) that fill the believer's scroll with good deeds.
